findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator allows negative-offset DB slicing
findings.body: In OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result, when enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, the code sets start_offset = cursor.offset (negative) and slices queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing and raise AssertionError, so a crafted cursor string like "0:-5:0" causes a 500/DoS. The comment claiming Django handles negative slicing automatically is false, and other paginators in the same file explicitly reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError.

findings.title: Hidden optimized_pagination flag switches to vulnerable paginator
findings.body: The endpoint adds an undocumented ?optimized_pagination=true query param that, for any superuser or member with has_global_access, switches from DateTimePaginator to OptimizedCursorPaginator with enable_advanced_features=True. This exposes the negative-offset path to a broad set of users on a sensitive audit-log endpoint with no tests or validation, widening attack surface unrelated to the spans-buffer title.

findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offset for prev cursors
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result was changed from queryset[offset:stop] to start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. For is_prev cursors the offset is used unclamped, so a client-supplied cursor with negative offset and is_prev=1 still reaches queryset[negative:stop]. This is inconsistent with OffsetPaginator/ChainPaginator which reject negative offsets, and causes AssertionError or undefined paging.

findings.title: Mandatory end_timestamp_precise lookup crashes consumer on missing field
findings.body: process_batch now does val["end_timestamp_precise"] with direct dict access. Any span event missing that field raises KeyError inside the Arroyo batch, failing the whole batch, blocking commits and causing consumer crash-loop/backlog instead of skipping or defaulting. Previously Span did not require the field.

findings.title: ZUNIONSTORE without AGGREGATE MAX corrupts scores on duplicates
findings.body: The migration from SUNIONSTORE to ZUNIONSTORE uses default SUM aggregation. If the same payload member exists in both source sets (retry, duplicate ingest, overlapping parent/span buffers), its score (end_timestamp_precise) is summed to 2x timestamp, corrupting ordering and future ZPOPMIN eviction victims. Should use AGGREGATE MAX.

findings.title: max_segment_spans enforcement removed, truncation is silent
findings.body: _load_segment_data no longer checks max_segment_spans, drops the segment_span_count_exceeded metric and error log, and leaves max_segment_spans config unused. Oversized segments are now silently truncated to 1000 in Lua via ZPOPMIN (hardcoded, off-by-one vs 1001 default) and flushed as incomplete instead of being skipped/logged, causing silent span loss.

findings.title: Redirect traversal cut from 10000 to 1000 fragments deep traces
findings.body: The redirect-following loop was reduced from 10000 to 1000 iterations. Traces/segment trees deeper than 1000 will stop early with an unresolved set_span_id, so spans that should merge into one segment stay in separate Redis keys and flush as fragmented segments. This is a correctness regression for deep traces to save Lua time.
